A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Engorgio study. The main text, Appendices A and B, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on six base models and seven supervised fine-tuned models, including ablations, transfer attacks, defense evaluations, and cloud-service measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The proxy distribution, Gumbel-Softmax construction, EOS escape and self-mentor losses, prompt sampling, and semantic-prefix variants are unchanged. Equations 2–7 retain the same method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Stanford-Alpaca and ShareGPT inputs, translation prompt scenarios, and multilingual Open-Platypus defense study. No dataset, task, or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: normal inputs, special inputs, LLMEffiChecker, and sponge examples where originally included. Citation changes do not change comparator participation.

E3.justification: Model configurations, context limits, metrics, optimization settings, temperature sweeps, and cloud-service controls remain unchanged. The new model-resource links document retained experiments rather than establish different settings.

E4.justification: The loss and prompt-length ablations, temperature and prefix/suffix analyses, transferability investigations, response distributions, cloud-service case study, and perplexity-filter evaluation are all retained with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions describe averaging sampled responses and typically using 100 samples in Appendix A.5. No new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted data, and qualitative examples are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains LLaMA-30B Engorgio results of 2019.1 Avg-len and 95% Avg-rate, and Table 15 retains the same four false-positive rates.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, complexity discussion, and latency derivation in Appendix A.5 are unchanged, including Equations 8–9. No theorem, proof, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about inducing long responses and threatening service availability. The stated 13-model coverage and roughly 2–13-fold effects are unchanged.

C2.justification: The new Ethics Statement explicitly qualifies the real-world demonstration as targeting only the authors' own service without affecting others. Mechanistic interpretations and Section 5 limitations remain unchanged; the proposed stress-testing application already appeared in Appendix A.2.

D1.justification: Table 5 gains direct model-resource links, including a specific Orca-mini-v3-7B checkpoint link. A new reproducibility statement describes evaluation code and a future full release, but its anonymous-repository wording conflicts with the retained public code link. No implementation change or actual change in code availability is established.

R1.justification: Several scholarly model citations, including the OPT, LLaMA-2, and Orca papers, are removed and replaced with model-resource footnotes. Other references, such as the Vicuna and Alpaca resources, simply move to footnotes. Positioning against previous inference-cost attacks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds ethics, reproducibility, and acknowledgments sections, changes the publication header and author order, and makes limited sentence and bibliography edits. The scientific narrative and section organization are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: All 11 figures and 16 tables remain. Some figures are resized, appendix displays reflow, Table 5 uses resource footnotes instead of inline citations, and the Figure 2 and Table 7 captions are shortened. The displayed scientific content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility through more specific model-resource identification, particularly the Orca checkpoint, and clarifies the controlled scope of the service demonstration. These gains are limited because the scientific evidence is unchanged. The inconsistent anonymous-repository and future-release wording weakens the new reproducibility statement but does not outweigh the modest documentation benefits.
